claim: Villa Pisani museum opens Tue-Sun 9:00-20:00; ticket €9 full, €6 reduced, €2 youth 18-25; park and maze closed until June 2026 for PNRR restoration.

claim: The Apotheosis of the Pisani Family by Giambattista Tiepolo (1760-62), in the ballroom of Villa Pisani Stra, is Tiepolo's largest fresco for a private residence and his last work in Italy.
quote: The Apotheosis of the Pisani Family, Giambattista Tiepolo's masterpiece decorating the ballroom of Villa Pisani in Stra, is his largest fresco painting for a private residence.

claim: Villa Pisani was begun in 1721 by the Pisani di Santo Stefano; Napoleon bought it in the early 19th century and famously got lost in the boxwood labyrinth in 1807.
quote: Villa Pisani, erected beginning in 1721 ... Napoleon Bonaparte purchased the villa ... in 1807, got completely lost in the labyrinth and had to be rescued by his guards.

claim: Villa Barbarigo's Baroque garden was commissioned 1669, voted Italy's most beautiful garden in 2003; its boxwood labyrinth uses ~6,000 plants mostly planted 1664-1669, making it one of the oldest surviving mazes.
quote: The baroque garden of the Villa Barbarigo has been voted as 'Italy's most beautiful garden' in 2003 ... The labyrinth is comprised of six thousand Boxwood plants, with the majority of these plants being over 400 years old as they were planted between 1664-1669
